svg.text: MPx Boil-Trap: portable boil, catch and cool (v0.3)
Boil 0.5 L on a small 600 W heater, flip the bottle, and gravity pulls the water through a steel mesh catcher into a metal cooling chamber. No circuit board, battery or app: one timer knob.
A · The unit, upright for boiling (section)
Ø115 × 330 mm · ~0.95 kg · 0.5 L per batch
Section, not to scale. Shown upright: boil chamber down, cooling chamber up.
B · Using it: four steps, ~10 min to treated water
C · All the electrics (no PCB, no battery)
below 100 °C the thermostat shorts the diode: full 600 W
at the boil it opens: the diode passes half-waves, ~300 W simmer
Eight electrical parts, all off-the-shelf kettle and oven spares. The
timer sets total time; the 100 °C thermostat on the chamber wall
switches boil to simmer by itself.
Energy per 0.5 L batch: ~66 Wh (≈ ₹0.5 of electricity). Steam lost in
Off-grid option later: a 12 V 150 W car-socket heater instead (≈ 3×
Two independent cut-offs (130 °C thermostat, 172 °C fuse) for boil-dry.
Earthed metal body, IEC 60335-2-15 (kettles) is the reference standard.
D · Prototype now from stock parts (big is fine)
3" (76 mm) SS316 tri-clamp spools, end caps, clamps, gaskets
Mechanical 15 min timer, KSD301 ×2, TCO, diode, fuse, rocker,
1/4" SS check valve as rollover vent
Clip-on fin sleeve (cut Al heat-sink) + silicone grip
Bimetal dial thermometer, TC fit (for tests)
3D-printed base housing, welding of the boss
≈ ₹10,000 total, about a quarter of the v0.2 bench rig
E · What the numbers say (sims H1–H5) and how it meets the requirements
bowl of tap water, refill once: ~16 min
lime per batch at 180 mg/L: ~80 mg
drains in ~1–5 min as the cake builds
12.5 µm+ settles in 3 min if you wait
rinse the mesh after each batch
Portable form (45% of quiz); ~19 parts, just inside req 9.2 (≤ 20); product
16.1); prototype ~₹10k (req 16.3); no plastic on the wet side (req 5.1/5.2).
Removal still needs hard water (~285 mg/L for 90%, req 10.1). Needs mains
power (req 4.4 only if classed portable). Cooling is slow without a water
bowl. Flipping hot water needs a drop and lock test.
Continuous 3–5 L/h flow, the on-device display and the heat-recovery
exchanger. Detection stays in the phone clip-on (Concept 05); the used mesh is

1) Lime formed in the vented chamber at 4 min, by titration, at 80/180/300 mg/L. 2) Mesh drain time per batch and after 10 batches. 3) Bead removal with Nile Red counts (Concept 05). 4) Rollover vent: no leak when flipped at 95 °C. 5) Surface temps
on the grip band and fin sleeve right after the flip (fins start near 90 °C: label 'hold the band').
